findings.title: Food pantry burns down at South Philly Community Fridge in Point Breeze
findings.exact_supporting_passage: South Philadelphia Community Fridge will operate without a pantry in its Point Breeze location for the foreseeable future
findings.summary: A fire on the evening of October 26 destroyed the wooden free-food pantry at the South Philadelphia Community Fridge's Point Breeze site at 19th and Ellsworth streets in Philadelphia. Local reporting published October 27 quotes a volunteer saying this particularly heavily used pantry will remain absent pending an investigation. The adjacent functioning fridge remains open and is accepting nonperishable food as a temporary substitute; thus this is a partial on-site food-access capacity loss, not a complete shutdown of the food distribution point. Replacement materials have reportedly been funded, but restoration timing is not established.
findings.location: Point Breeze, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (19th and Ellsworth streets)
findings.scope: One community-fridge network location; loss of standalone pantry storage, with adjacent fridge continuing to operate

Twelve targeted web searches completed across four designated classes. One newly discovered current-day report met the facility-damage pantry-access-loss criterion; not claimed to be published after the last hourly heartbeat, because only a day-level article date was displayed.

PhillyVoice's October 27 report documented destruction of a wooden food pantry at Point Breeze by a Monday evening fire and confirmed the remaining refrigerator is still operational as a temporary alternative. The affected site was described by a volunteer as among the network's most heavily used locations. This is a bounded loss of on-site pantry capacity, not complete termination of food service.

Provider website corroborates operating location at 1840 Ellsworth Street but no primary-source incident notice was located within the bounded searches. Editorial review should confirm service impact and restoration timetable before consideration for publication.

No other verified within-window only/last grocery loss, canceled storm/disaster distribution, or official current SNAP/WIC interruption surfaced. Search results for SNAP disruptions were predominantly from 2025; older closure stories and the previously logged Wymore, Nebraska and Heber City/Provo, Utah reports were not duplicated.
